_meta.indication: Topical treatment of moderate to severe chronic hand eczema (CHE) in adults who have had an inadequate response to, or for whom topical corticosteroids are not advisable

pivotal_trials.population: Adults 18 years and older with moderate to severe chronic hand eczema (IGA-CHE score of 3 or 4) with inadequate response to, or for whom topical corticosteroids were not advisable
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of subjects who achieved IGA-CHE treatment success (IGA-CHE TS) at Week 16, defined as a score of 0 or 1 with at least a 2-point improvement from baseline
pivotal_trials.result: IGA-CHE TS at Week 16: 20% (64/325) ANZUPGO vs 10% (16/162) vehicle; difference from vehicle 10% (95% CI 4%, 16%)

pivotal_trials.population: Adults 18 years and older with moderate to severe chronic hand eczema (IGA-CHE score of 3 or 4) with inadequate response to, or for whom topical corticosteroids were not advisable
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of subjects who achieved IGA-CHE treatment success (IGA-CHE TS) at Week 16, defined as a score of 0 or 1 with at least a 2-point improvement from baseline
pivotal_trials.result: IGA-CHE TS at Week 16: 29% (91/313) ANZUPGO vs 7% (11/159) vehicle; difference from vehicle 22% (95% CI 16%, 29%)

key_safety: Higher rates in delgocitinib vs vehicle: COVID-19 (11.1% vs 10.6%), upper respiratory tract infection (1.4% vs 0.3%), hypertension (1.1% vs 0%), back pain (1.1% vs 0.3%); serious infections including eczema herpeticum reported
target_moa: Delgocitinib is a Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitor that inhibits the activity of JAK1, JAK2, JAK3, and TYK2; JAK signaling recruits STATs to cytokine receptors to induce expression of cytokine-responsive genes

advisory_committee.vote: No Advisory Committee meeting was held because the review team identified no unexpected or significant safety/efficacy issue or controversial/challenging issue warranting external discussion

basis.text: FDA granted fast track designation for delgocitinib cream in the treatment of moderate to severe CHE on June 12, 2020

basis.text: Priority review was requested with this NDA but denied because the Applicant did not provide clinical evidence indicating that the drug demonstrates substantial improvement over existing therapies on one or more clinically significant efficacy or safety endpoints; standard review clock followed

citations.quote: The Applicant requested priority review designation with this NDA; however, that request was denied.

The Agency denied the priority review request because the Applicant did not provide clinical evidence indicating that the drug demonstrates substantial improvement over existing therapies on one or more clinically significant efficacy or safety endpoints.

summary.text: ANZUPGO received fast track designation (June 12, 2020); breakthrough therapy and priority review requests were both denied, so the NDA underwent standard review supported by two adequate and well-controlled Phase 3 trials (DELTA 1 and DELTA 2)

citations.quote: The U.S. FDA granted fast track designation for the investigation of delgocitinib cream in the treatment of moderate to severe CHE on June 12, 2020, following a fast-track request submission on May 5, 2020.
The Applicant requested priority review designation with this NDA; however, that request was denied.

The Applicant provided substantial evidence of effectiveness with data from two adequate and well-controlled trials, DELTA 1 and DELTA 2, that evaluated delgocitinib cream, 2% twice daily (BID) compared with vehicle for 16 weeks.
